title: Canonical MariaDB utf8mb4 search-token index exceeds InnoDB key budget

actualExecution.error: Specified key was too long; max key length is 3072 bytes

rootCause: The canonical schema did not model MariaDB utf8mb4 index byte budgets. The first actual failure was a full composite index over an HMAC-SHA256 search token using its generic 1000-character storage bound; after adding a generic fail-closed calculation, the gate exposed at least one additional oversized composite index. The defect is repository-wide canonical index sizing, not a single table exception.
runtimeContract: JceCpfCryptoOperations.searchableToken emits lowercase HMAC-SHA256 hex (64 characters). Full column storage remains compatible; MariaDB may safely index a bounded prefix and the equality predicate still validates the complete token.
repair: Add a MariaDB vendor index prefix within 3072 bytes at the canonical schema owner, add a generic fail-closed MariaDB index-budget gate, regenerate current DB3 source/install packs, and publish a new append-only V135/R135 repair for already-installed schemas without modifying V102 or any existing checksum.

sourceFixAttempt1.gateAdded: generic MariaDB utf8mb4 byte-budget calculation for canonical unique/index definitions

sourceFixAttempt2.gateReporting: Every collected canonical DDL safety error is emitted with ErrorAction Continue before the aggregate failure is raised.

sourceFixAttempt3.canonicalDesign: GW_BINDING stores one non-null CHAR(64) binding_key_hash and the unique constraint owns that bounded digest instead of a lossy prefix over six long fields.
sourceFixAttempt3.digestContract: SHA-256 over the concatenation of six per-component SHA-256 hexadecimal digests: environment, host pattern, path pattern, normalized HTTP method, API version, route version.
sourceFixAttempt3.runtimeOwner: JdbcCpfGatewayRegistryAdapter writes the digest on insert and update; CpfGatewayRoute normalizes blank HTTP method to the persisted wildcard.
sourceFixAttempt3.regression: Canonical cross-vendor renderer assertion plus Java deterministic/full-field/wildcard normalization tests added.

migrationAuthoring.forward: six normalized full UTF-8 components -> per-component SHA-256 -> outer SHA-256; unique bounded CHAR(64)
migrationAuthoring.rollback: data-preserving nullable digest plus compatibility write trigger; no lossy prefix unique and no column/data deletion

passCriteria: canonical safety gate rejects any MariaDB utf8mb4 index above 3072 encoded bytes
current MariaDB Fresh DDL uses a valid prefix index while PostgreSQL/Oracle retain full index semantics
V102 and all pre-existing Migration/Rollback bytes remain unchanged
new V135/R135 is append-only and registered without changing prior manifest prefixes
actual MariaDB Fresh Upgrade Rollback Reapply lifecycle passes and cleanup passes
